newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends 7.57 pct up on peso plunge.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends 7.57 pct up on peso plunge.

text.p: The Philippine stock market's main index bounced back on Friday by 189.99 points, or 7.57 percent, to 2,701.14 points, posting the biggest single-day rise in percentage terms in nearly seven years.
The surge came after the Central Bank said it was allowing the peso to trade in a wider range, which effectively meant a devaluation of the peso.

"It eased the tension among investors in the equities market. All they really wanted was for the peso to seek its own levels," said Cora Guidote, head of Philippine equities at UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd.

"The peso was allowed to depreciate so finally much of the uncertainty that had caused the market to drop in the last few days has been removed," David de la Cruz, Amsteel Securities Corp vice-president for marketing said.
The main index on Friday snapped out of a four day losing streak.
"The market was trying to preempt a possible lowering of overnight rates as a result of the Central Bank's move," said Cilette Liboro, research of head at Orion-Squire Capital.
